programs.name: Amyloid
programs.goal: Clear amyloid early enough to change the course of the disease.

programs.name: Tau
programs.goal: Stop tau spreading between connected brain regions.

programs.name: Immune
programs.goal: Turn microglia and inflammation from harmful to protective.

programs.name: APOE
programs.goal: Neutralise the biggest common genetic risk, APOE4.

programs.name: Vascular
programs.goal: Protect blood flow, the blood-brain barrier and waste clearance.

programs.name: Metabolic
programs.goal: Fix how the ageing brain uses fuel.

programs.name: Infection
programs.goal: Test whether viruses or bacteria help trigger the disease.

programs.name: Detection
programs.goal: Find the disease years earlier with a blood draw.

programs.name: Prevention
programs.goal: Delay onset through risk factors anyone can change.

programs.name: Synapse
programs.goal: Keep synapses working even with pathology present.

claims.text: Lecanemab slows decline in early Alzheimer's, about 27% on CDR-SB over 18 months (CLARITY AD); full FDA approval.
Donanemab slows decline in early symptomatic Alzheimer's (TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2); FDA approval.
Clearing amyloid before symptoms prevents them (AHEAD 3-45, TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 3 running).
BACE inhibitors slow decline by cutting amyloid production; verubecestat and others failed, some worsened cognition.
Gamma-secretase inhibition slows decline; semagacestat worsened cognition and was halted.
Solanezumab prevents decline in preclinical Alzheimer's (A4 study missed).
Gantenerumab slows decline in early Alzheimer's (GRADUATE I and II missed).
Aducanumab gives clinical benefit; Biogen discontinued it after accelerated approval.
Aβ*56 oligomer causes memory loss; the 2006 Nature paper was retracted.
Tau PET spread tracks symptoms more closely than amyloid load.
N-terminal anti-tau antibodies slow decline (semorinemab, gosuranemab missed).
Lowering tau production with antisense (BIIB080) slows decline; phase 2 running.
Mid-domain antibodies block tau seeding between neurons.
TREM2 variants raise Alzheimer's risk, implicating microglia.
TREM2 agonist antibody AL002 slows decline (INVOKE-2 missed).
Systemic inflammation accelerates progression.
APOE4 homozygosity is a distinct genetic form of Alzheimer's, with near-complete pathology by 65.
APOE4 is the largest common genetic risk factor for late-onset Alzheimer's.
APOE genotype stratifies ARIA risk before antibody dosing.
The APOE Christchurch variant protects against early-onset disease (rare case reports).
Intensive blood-pressure control lowers risk of mild cognitive impairment (SPRINT MIND).
Blood-brain barrier breakdown in APOE4 carriers precedes decline; replication running.
Failing glymphatic clearance during sleep drives amyloid build-up.
Oral semaglutide slows early Alzheimer's (EVOKE and EVOKE+ missed despite biomarker shifts).
Brain insulin resistance drives the disease ("type 3 diabetes").
Ketone supply rescues glucose hypometabolism.
Shingles vaccination lowers dementia risk (Wales natural experiment); replication running.
Gingipain inhibitor atuzaginstat slows decline (GAIN missed co-primary endpoints).
HSV-1 reactivation seeds amyloid as an antimicrobial response.
Plasma pTau217/Aβ42 ratio detects amyloid; Lumipulse cleared by FDA.
Single-biomarker plasma pTau217 rules amyloid in or out; Elecsys cleared by FDA.
Amyloid changes begin 15 to 20 years before symptoms (DIAN).
Blood tests can screen symptom-free adults (not cleared for this use).
14 modifiable risk factors account for about 45% of dementia (Lancet Commission).
A structured multidomain lifestyle programme slows decline (US POINTER); replication running.
Hearing aids slow decline in higher-risk older adults (ACHIEVE subgroup only).
Simufilam restores filamin A and slows decline; ReThink-ALZ failed and the programme ended.
Synaptic resilience explains why some people with plaques never develop dementia.
